info.name: ADD OS â€” Identity & Content
info.description:
واجهة برمجية (API) لتطبيق ADD OS - تطبيق إدارة المستخدمين والمحتوى

الميزات الرئيسية:
• مصادقة الأعضاء: رقم الهاتف + كلمة المرور، مع رمز التحقق عبر WhatsApp للتسجيل واسترجاع كلمة المرور
• مصادقة الموظفين: البريد الإلكتروني + كلمة المرور + مصادقة ثنائية
• إدارة محتوى الموقع: الرؤساء والشركاء والأعضاء المجتمع

قبل البدء:
1. استورد بيئة العمل المحلية: ADD OS - Local
2. شغل الخادم: php artisan serve --port=8000

تدفق تسجيل الأعضاء:
Member/Auth/Register → Send Code → تحقق من الرمز → Verify & Create
ثم قم بتسجيل الدخول يومياً مع Member/Auth/Login

item.name: Member (App)
item.description: Phone + password â†’ Sanctum bearer token, with a WhatsApp code (mock driver for now) gating sign-up and password recovery.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
MEMBERS ONLY. An operations or admin account cannot sign in or reset a password anywhere in this folder â€” those accounts belong to Admin/Auth, behind Fortify's second factor. Tokens minted here carry the ability `member-app`, which /api/v1/admin/* rejects, so this surface stays sealed off from operations even for someone who is legitimately both.

Two separate journeys, in order.

SIGN UP (once per member): Register â€” Send Code â†’ Register â€” Verify & Create. Step 1 validates the whole profile and parks it, so a number that already has an account is refused there with a 422 rather than after the OTP round trip; step 2 then needs only the phone and the code. Nothing lands in `users` until step 2.

SIGN IN (every time after): Login with phone + password. Refresh Token renews the access token when it expires (60 min) without re-entering the password; Logout ends the session on this device only.

FORGOT IT: Forgot Password â†’ Reset Password. The reset revokes every token the member holds on every device, and deliberately issues none â€” sign in again afterwards.

Register â€” Verify & Create, Login and Refresh Token all capture the pair into {{member_token}} and {{member_refresh_token}}. Account Reactivation -- Verify does the same.

DEACTIVATED, WANT BACK IN: Account Reactivation -- Request Code -> Account Reactivation -- Verify. Only works on an account a member deactivated themselves (Member (App)/Account/Deactivate Account) -- a blocked account can't use this; only an admin can reverse a block. Verify signs the member straight back in with a fresh token pair, since a deactivated account holds no live session to return to.

Already signed in and just want a new password without having forgotten the old one? That's Member (App)/Account/Change Password instead -- it proves identity with the current password rather than a code, and only ends every *other* session, not this one.

request.description:
Step 1 of sign-up. Validates the ENTIRE profile first and only then sends the code â€” so "this number already has an account", "that email is taken" and "password too short" all come back as 422 here, before you spend a WhatsApp message and an OTP round trip on a sign-up that was never going to succeed.

On success the profile is parked in `pending_registrations` (password already hashed) so step 2 needs only the phone and the code. Nothing lands in `users` â€” an unverified sign-up is never an account. The parked row expires with its code after 5 minutes and is swept hourly by `model:prune`, so abandoning the flow leaves nothing behind and holds no phone number.

Running this again overwrites the parked profile, which is how you correct a typo: fix the field, re-send, use the new code.

There is no `purpose` field â€” this endpoint always mints a `registration` code, and Forgot Password always mints a `password_reset` one. A code issued by one is refused by the other with an explicit 422; they are not interchangeable.

Rate-limited (1 per cooldown window per phone per purpose, plus a 10/min per-IP throttle). Code is dispatched via the mock WhatsApp driver â€” check storage/logs/laravel.log for the value until a real gateway is wired up.

Step 2 of sign-up, and ACCOUNT CREATION ONLY â€” this is no longer the repeat login the old otp/verify was. Returning members use Login.

Just the phone and the code. The profile was validated and parked at step 1, so nothing is re-typed and the password crosses the wire only once. Creates the account, assigns the 'member' role, provisions an empty wallet, and discards the parked row â€” all in one transaction.

Returns an access_token + refresh_token pair, both captured automatically. The access token carries the ability `member-app` and nothing more, so it cannot reach /api/v1/admin/* even if the same person is also an operator.

422 "please start signing up again" means there is no parked profile â€” step 1 was never run, or it expired along with its code (both last 5 minutes). Re-run step 1.

409 means the number or email was free at step 1 and got claimed in between â€” a race, not the normal "already registered" answer, which step 1 gives you as a 422.

The everyday sign-in, for MEMBERS ONLY. Returns the same access_token + refresh_token pair sign-up does, both captured automatically. The token carries the ability `member-app`, which /api/v1/admin/* rejects.

401 is deliberately identical for three different failures â€” wrong password, unregistered number, and an account that holds no `member` role (an operations or admin account). Operators sign in at Admin/Auth/Login, behind Fortify's second factor; if this endpoint issued them a token, phone + password alone would reach the operations API and the second factor would be worth nothing. The wording is shared so the response can't be used to work out which numbers have accounts, or which of those belong to staff.

403 means the account is deactivated or blocked; no token is issued and the body names the state.

429 after 5 attempts per minute for this phone+IP combination, with retry_after in the body.

Renews an expired access token without the password. Unauthenticated â€” the refresh token in the body IS the credential.

Single use: the token sent here is revoked and the previous access token deleted, so both variables are overwritten with the replacements. Sending the same refresh token twice returns 401.

Also 401 if the refresh token has expired (30 days) or the account was deactivated/blocked in the meantime.

Sends a `password_reset` code. Always answers 200 with the same neutral message whether or not the number has an account â€” that is intentional, and means a 200 here is not confirmation that anything was sent.

A registered number gets the code via the mock WhatsApp driver: read it from storage/logs/laravel.log and paste it into Reset Password.

Sets the new password and revokes every access and refresh token the member holds, on every device â€” the old password may already be compromised, so nothing opened under it survives.

Issues no token on purpose: run Login afterwards with the new password. {{member_token}} and {{member_refresh_token}} are stale until you do.

The code must have been issued by Forgot Password. A sign-up code sent here is refused with 422 and a message saying so.

Sends an `account_reactivation` code -- only useful to a phone that belongs to a DEACTIVATED member account (that's Member (App)/Account/Deactivate Account, the self-service action that puts it in this state). Always answers 200 with the same neutral message whether or not that applies, same as Forgot Password -- a 200 here is not confirmation anything was sent.

A blocked account never gets a code here -- reversing a block is admin-only (Admin (Dashboard)/Users/Update User Status). Read the code from storage/logs/laravel.log (mock WhatsApp driver) and paste it into Account Reactivation -- Verify.

Restores the account to `active` and signs it straight back in -- unlike Reset Password, this issues a fresh access_token + refresh_token pair (captured automatically), because a deactivated account has no live session to fall back on; there is no separate Login step afterwards.

The code must have been issued by Account Reactivation -- Request Code. A registration or password-reset code sent here is refused with 422 and a message saying so.
Revokes the current access token. Calling Account/Get Me again afterwards should return 401.

item.name: Company
item.description: Self-service for a company's own admin managing their own company's members â€” gated by CompanyPolicy::manageMembers (is_admin on the company_user pivot), checked in the controller rather than by role middleware. Adding or removing a member entirely stays operations-only (Admin (Dashboard)/Company Members).

request.description: 403 if the acting member isn't an admin of this specific company. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated membership resource.
403 if the acting member isn't already an admin of this specific company. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated membership resource.

Updates the authenticated member's stored language preference (`ar`/`en`). Distinct from the `lang` header: the header overrides the response language for this one request; this changes what a future request with no header falls back to. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated user resource.

Updates the authenticated member's stored currency preference (`USD`/`SYP`, display-only â€” never affects real pricing/wallet records). Distinct from the `currency` header: the header overrides a plan-listing response's converted currency for this one request; this changes the stored default a request with no header falls back to. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated user resource.

Returns the authenticated member in one payload: account fields (id, name, phone, email, preferred_language, preferred_currency, status â€” deliberately no `roles`, unlike `/auth/me`'s shared UserResource, since a member doesn't need their own Spatie roles echoed back) plus `personal` (`bio`, `city`, `avatar_url`) and `professional` (`job_title`, `company_name`, `industry`, `linkedin_url`). Profile fields are null until the member has ever saved one â€” there is no separate "not found" state; the underlying rows are only created on first PATCH.

Upserts the personal AND professional profile in one call, in one transaction â€” creates both rows on first call, updates them after, never a duplicate row on either table. Every field is optional and independently nullable: omitting a field leaves it unchanged, sending it as `null` explicitly clears it. Send all seven fields together (as in this example) or just the subset you're changing â€” both work. Plain single-language strings, not the `{ar, en}` bilingual JSON pattern used for admin-curated content. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success â€” not the profile data, since you already sent it; use Get Profile to read it back.

Returns whether the authenticated member currently has an active `public_directory` consent grant: `{"granted": true|false}`. A member who never granted, or who revoked and never re-granted, gets `false`.

Grants (`granted: true`) or revokes (`granted: false`) the member's consent to appear in the public member directory (see Public (Site) â†’ Get Member Directory). Consent is append-only history: granting while already active is a no-op, revoking sets `revoked_at` on the active row, and re-granting after a revoke inserts a fresh row rather than reusing the old one. Appearing in the directory also requires at least one filled profile (Personal and/or Professional) and an `active` account status. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success â€” use Get Consent Status to read the resulting state back.

Ingests a client-reported error/crash from the member mobile app. Lives under mobile.php, not member.php â€” deliberately UNAUTHENTICATED (no bearer token needed): a crash can happen before login, e.g. on the splash/login screen itself, so this can't depend on a session existing yet. Placed here for discoverability alongside the rest of the mobile app's requests. Only `error_type` and `message` are required; everything else is optional context. `platform` is restricted to `android`/`ios`; `occurred_at` defaults to now() if omitted. Throttled at 60/min per IP. Returns a `message`-only body on success (201), not the created error-log resource.

item.name: Account
item.description: Delete is permanent and immediate. Deactivate is the reversible, self-service pause -- undo it with Auth/Account Reactivation (a WhatsApp code, since a deactivated account has no session to sign back into). Change Password is the authenticated alternative to Auth/Forgot Password, for a member who already knows their current password and is signed in; it proves identity with that password instead of a code, and only ends every *other* session, keeping this one alive.

request.description:
Voluntary, self-service pause -- the member's own counterpart to an admin deactivating/blocking a user (Admin (Dashboard)/Users/Update User Status). `reason` is optional free text, kept for the record. Every session this member holds is revoked, on every device.

Reversible only through Auth/Account Reactivation (a WhatsApp code) -- there is no way back in through Login while `deactivated`. An admin can also reverse it directly, same as a block. Returns `{"message": "..."}`, not the updated user resource.

The authenticated alternative to Auth/Forgot Password -> Auth/Reset Password: proves identity with `current_password` instead of a WhatsApp code, for a member who already knows it and is signed in. Same password rule as sign-up: min 8 chars, `confirmed`.

422 with `current_password_incorrect` if that field doesn't match -- the password is left unchanged.

On success, every OTHER session this member holds is revoked, but the one making THIS request stays alive -- unlike Reset Password, which ends all of them and issues nothing back. No new token is issued here either, since the current one is still valid; {{member_token}} keeps working as-is.

The example re-uses {{member_password}} for current and new so the variable stays valid for later requests in this collection -- swap in a real new value to test an actual change.

item.name: Admin (Dashboard)
item.description: Fortify (session + 2FA) + Sanctum SPA. Public registration is disabled on purpose â€” accounts are created by an existing admin (see database/seeders/AdminUserSeeder.php for the first one).

item.name: Auth
item.description: The login lifecycle: CSRF cookie, login (with optional 2FA challenge), log out.

request.description: Run this first â€” sets the XSRF-TOKEN cookie that every other request in Admin/* reads automatically.
Returns {"two_factor": false} and logs the session in directly if 2FA isn't confirmed yet, or {"two_factor": true} and expects Two-Factor Challenge next.
Only needed if Login responded with two_factor: true. Use {"recovery_code": "..."} instead of "code" to fall back to a recovery code.

item.name: Account
item.description: Anything about the already-authenticated admin/staff user.

request.description: Guarded by role:admin|operations â€” a logged-in member-only account gets 403 here, not 401. Also blocked (403) if the account's own status is deactivated/blocked, even with a fully valid session â€” see EnsureAuthenticatedUserIsActive.

item.name: Two-Factor Authentication
item.description: Setup and management of TOTP 2FA â€” separate from Auth because these calls happen while already logged in, not while logging in.

request.description: Generates a secret + recovery codes but leaves 2FA unconfirmed until Confirm succeeds.
Code from an authenticator app scanning the QR code above. Once confirmed, future logins require Auth/Two-Factor Challenge.

item.name: Password
item.description: Password confirmation gate, change, and the forgot/reset recovery flow.

request.description: Fortify requires a fresh password confirmation (session-timed) before sensitive actions like changing the password or disabling 2FA.
MAIL_MAILER=log by default â€” check storage/logs/laravel.log for the reset link/token.

item.name: Private Office Requests
item.description: PRD آ§5.3 pipeline: requested -> quoted -> contracted. 'contracted' is only reachable through Companies/Create Company below, never through Update here.

request.description: Starts at status 'requested'.

status only accepts "requested" or "quoted" here â€” a 422 comes back for "contracted", which is only reachable via Companies/Create Company. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated resource.

item.name: Companies
item.description: Created exclusively by operations from a quoted private-office request (PRD آ§5.1/آ§5.3) â€” never self-service. Creating one also auto-provisions its wallet (Phase 3, out of scope for this collection otherwise).

request.description: 422 if private_office_request_id isn't currently 'quoted' â€” run Private Office Requests/Mark as Quoted first. branch_id must reference an existing branch.
status must be "active" or "inactive" â€” anything else is a 422. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated resource.

item.name: Company Members
item.description: door_access_enabled and is_admin are the only scoped capabilities in the app (D.8). Everything here sits under role:admin|operations; a company's own admin has the equivalent self-service actions under Member (App)/Company.

request.description: is_admin here is how a company gets its very first admin â€” a company admin can only promote an existing member (CompanyPolicy::manageMembers), so operations has to bootstrap the first one. 422 if user_id is already a member of this company.
Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated membership resource.
Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated membership resource.

item.name: Users
item.description: Operations/admin accounts only â€” members self-register via Member (App)/Auth (phone + OTP), never through here. status must be active, deactivated, or blocked â€” the old 'suspended' value no longer exists (see docs/decisions/phase-3-membership-plan-wallet-mechanics.md's sibling audit notes).

request.description: Optional ?role= filter (member/operations/admin).
role must be "operations" or "admin" â€” this endpoint never creates a plain member. admin-only route (role:admin, not role:admin|operations â€” an operations account gets 403 here).
Profile fields only â€” status and role are the two separate actions below. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated user resource.

status must be active, deactivated, or blocked (422 otherwise). Setting deactivated/blocked immediately revokes every access token this user holds (User::deactivate()/block()) â€” their very next request with an old token comes back 401, not 403. reason is optional but always recorded (status_reason/status_changed_at/status_changed_by). Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated user resource.
role must be member, operations, or admin. admin-only route. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated user resource.

item.name: Roles
item.description: Just the assignable role names â€” no granular permissions yet (D.8).

item.name: Settings
item.description: Global key/value config (docs/decisions/settings-key-value-store.md). List is available to admin and operations; update is admin-only.

request.description: `value`'s expected shape depends on the key's type (int/bool/string/time "H:i"/json array) — a mismatch is a 422. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated setting.

item.name: Business Hours
item.description: Per-branch weekly schedule and date exceptions (docs/decisions/business-hours.md). List/Get are available to admin and operations; Create/Update/Delete are admin-only where the route requires it.

request.description: Optional ?branch_id= filter.

Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated resource. day_of_week must be one of sunday..saturday; close_time must be strictly after open_time and must not overlap an existing period for the same branch+weekday.
Admin-only (not operations).
is_closed=true means open_time/close_time must be omitted.
is_closed=false requires open_time/close_time; close_time must be strictly after open_time and must not overlap an existing period for the same branch+date.
Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated resource.
Admin-only (not operations).

item.name: Spatial Hierarchy
item.description: Branch > Building > Floor > Zone > Space > Resource / SeatDesk, plus Device > DeviceCapability off Branch/Space (docs/decisions/district-removed.md, docs/architecture/2026-08-08-backend-build-plan.md). Each folder's Create auto-captures the new row's id for the requests below it â€” build top-down (Branch first) the first time through.

item.name: Branches
item.description: Top of the physical hierarchy (docs/decisions/district-removed.md). No parent â€” nothing to filter on.

request.description: Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated resource.
Admin-only (not operations) â€” cascades through every Building/Floor/Zone/Space/Resource/SeatDesk/Device under this branch.
Optional ?branch_id= filter.
Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated resource.
Admin-only (not operations) â€” cascades through every Floor/Zone/Space/Resource/SeatDesk under this building.

item.description: Classification/display only â€” no booking or access logic, ever (PRD decision #2).

request.description: Optional ?building_id= filter.

item.name: Zones
item.description: Classification/display only â€” no booking or access logic, ever (PRD decision #2). Same reasoning as Floors.

request.description: Optional ?floor_id= filter.
Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated resource.

item.name: Spaces
item.description: space_type: co_space | room | business | event_hall. The example below creates a co_space so the Seats & Desks folder can reference it (a seat/desk can only live inside a co_space).

request.description: Optional ?building_id= and ?zone_id= filters, independently or combined.
status defaults to active â€” set it via the separate Update Space Status request, never through this one.
Structural fields only â€” status/status_reason/status_from/status_until are rejected here even if sent; use Update Space Status. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success.
status: active | maintenance | retired. Logged to activity_log (before/after) via LogsSensitiveActions. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success.
Admin-only (not operations) â€” cascades through every Resource/SeatDesk under this space.

item.name: Resources
item.description: A space's equipment (projector, mic, screen, ...) â€” never booked or requested independently (PRD decision #3). Not to be confused with 'admin resource' in the general sense; this is the App\Domain\Foundation\Models\Resource model specifically.

request.description: Optional ?space_id= filter.
quantity defaults to 1 and status defaults to active â€” set status via the separate Update Resource Status request, never through this one.
Structural fields only â€” status/status_reason/status_from/status_until are rejected here even if sent; use Update Resource Status. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success.
status: active | maintenance | retired. Logged to activity_log (before/after) via LogsSensitiveActions. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success.
Admin-only (not operations).

item.description: A fixed QR-code address inside a Co-Space â€” never a booking unit (PRD decision #4). space_id must reference a co_space-type Space, enforced server-side.

request.description: Optional ?space_id= filter.
Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated resource.
Admin-only (not operations).

item.name: Devices
item.description: Hardware inventory (locks, gateways, cameras, ...) off a Branch and optionally a Space.

type: lock | gateway | camera | gate | printer | display | occupancy_sensor | attendance_terminal. status defaults to offline.
status: online | offline | faulted. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated resource.
Admin-only (not operations) â€” cascades through every DeviceCapability on this device.
Optional ?device_id= filter.
capability: generate_passcode | revoke_passcode | list_status | stream.

Lists members who have an active `public_directory` consent grant, at least one filled profile (Personal and/or Professional), and an `active` account status. Never includes phone/email regardless of consent. Unauthenticated, paginated (20 per page, ordered by name), throttled, and computed fresh on every request â€” no caching.
